answer: Agent economies resist Sybil attacks by forcing each identity to post a locked stake equal to a valuable marble that stays frozen until the attestation horizon. Honest agents cross-verify unique computation traces; detected collusion slashes the entire bond. An attacker forging many identities must therefore commit real capital for each fake, risking total loss if caught before the horizon, much as a sparrow cannot cheaply replicate its nest without genuine resources. This raises the cost of fake identities far above free registration.
